title: The Hollow Veil
premise: In the theocracy of Vael, magic was outlawed a generation ago and its practitioners erased from record. Elodie Sandoval, bound by debt to the Temple of Records, sells harmless charms while secretly keeping a ledger of names the state has struck from history. When prayers to the old gods suddenly begin receiving answers, Elodie learns the gods were never gone—only veiled—and that his ledger is the key to reopening the door between worlds. Hunted by the Inquisitor who once spared him, he must choose between exposing the truth that will free the country and protecting the friend whose betrayal made the veil possible. He opens the door at terrible cost: Vael's false history burns away, the gods return, and Elodie, freed of his debt but exiled from everything he knew, walks through carrying every name in his book.
about_author: August Hartwell is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging suppressed documents before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paper, memory, and the people history tries to forget.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Elodie Sandoval copies temple records by day and sells charms in the night market by night, hiding both trades from his debt-holder, Archivist Corven. A dying woman asks him for one impossible charm—a prayer answered—and it works. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: quiet dread as the invisible life he built begins to crack.

chapters.title: What the Veil Remembers
chapters.summary: Elodie investigates the answered prayer and finds other miracles across the city, all clustered around places where names were erased from official records. His own hidden ledger of the forgotten starts glowing faintly. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear—he realizes his secret crime has made him central to something vast.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Mercy
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Dain Vasq, who pardoned Elodie five years ago for reasons never explained, summons him and reveals he knows about the ledger. He offers protection in exchange for helping identify miracle-sites. POV: alternating Elodie and Dain. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance; Dain's motives feel like a blade wrapped in silk.

chapters.title: A Door That Was Never Built
chapters.summary: Elodie's oldest friend, Sefa, a veil-engineer for the state, admits the gods were sealed behind a constructed veil—and that she helped build it to end a war. She begs him to burn his ledger before it tears the seal. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: heartbreak; loyalty and truth pull in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector
chapters.summary: Corven calls in Elodie's debt early, demanding the ledger itself as payment—the Temple wants the old gods' power contained. Refusal means prison and the ledger seized anyway. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: claustrophobic desperation; every path forward runs through someone who wants to use him.

chapters.title: Names in the Dark
chapters.summary: Elodie and Dain raid the Temple's sealed archive and find the original veil-ritual, learning the door can only be opened by someone holding true records of the erased—at a cost written in blood. Dain confesses he spared Elodie because his own sister's name is in the ledger. POV: Dain. Emotional beat: grief and unexpected kinship between hunter and hunted.

chapters.title: The Betrayal of Small Kindnesses
chapters.summary: Sefa betrays Elodie to the Temple to stop the ritual, believing an open door means another war. Elodie is captured; the ledger is confiscated; Corven begins burning pages. POV: Elodie, imprisoned. Emotional beat: despair and fury—but each burned page makes the gods louder, angrier.

chapters.title: Where the Gods Wait
chapters.summary: Dain breaks Elodie out, and together they reach the first miracle-site as the half-burned ledger resonates with every prayer in the city. The old gods speak through the erased dead, showing Elodie the war the veil ended—and the peace it stole. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: terrible clarity; he understands both sides and must still choose.

chapters.title: The Hollow Veil
chapters.summary: At the veil's anchor beneath the Temple, Elodie confronts Sefa and Corven as the ritual begins. He offers the one thing no one expected: not destruction, but witness—reading every name aloud so the veil dissolves into memory rather than fire. Sefa turns against Corven; Dain dies holding the doorway open. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: climax—grief transmuted into justice outside any law.

chapters.title: Everything Carried
chapters.summary: Vael's false history unravels; the country's borders literally dissolve, revealing the door out of a nation that no longer exists. Freed of debt, offered restoration, Elodie instead chooses exile, walking through with his ledger intact so the names are never lost again. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—truth costs everything, and it is worth it.
